title: African flower — three colours
subtitle: A nine-petal hexagonal motif worked in three colours, 12 cm
excerpt: The African flower builds nine puff-stitch petals outward from a tight centre ring, then frames them with a single-colour hexagonal border. Three colours — centre, petals, and border — give the classic high-contrast graphic that tiles into throws, bags, and cushion covers without seams visible from the front.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from widely-documented African flower construction in DK-weight cotton. Weldon's Practical Crochet (1886, Internet Archive) for puff-stitch motif principles. The three-colour arrangement follows the standard published palette convention.
heroPrompt: An African flower three-colour crochet motif in sage green petals, cream centre, and warm terracotta border, photographed flat from above on natural linen in soft daylight. Hexagonal shape, 12 cm, nine petals visible, perfectly blocked.

chartDefinition.caption: Three rounds from the magic ring. Round 1 (Colour A): tight dc ring. Round 2 (Colour B): nine puff-stitch petals into alternate spaces. Round 3 (Colour C): hexagonal treble border into petal tips and chain arches.

glossaryTerms.definition: Several elongated half trebles worked into the same stitch and pulled together at the top. Produces a soft, rounded bump — the petal shape in the African flower.
A method for joining motifs during the final round of each new tile, by replacing a chain with a slip stitch into the neighbour. Leaves no seams on the front of the work.

content.text: petals in the second round, then closes them inside a hexagonal treble border. Three distinct yarn colours give the petals maximum contrast against both the centre and the border, which is why the classic three-colour version tiles so legibly in throws and bags.

A puff stitch is looser and rounder than a bobble: you draw up several elongated half-treble loops from the same stitch before pulling through them all at once. The height of the loops sets the petal height, so tension here affects the finished look more than any other round. Too tight and the petals lie flat; too loose and the motif cups. A 4 mm hook in DK cotton at normal tension gives petals that stand slightly above the border.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 3 g of Colour A (centre), 5 g of Colour B (petals), 6 g of Colour C (border) — all DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Each finished African flower measures 12 cm across flat sides (point to point 13.5 cm) in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a steam-block. Work one test motif before committing to a blanket grid.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
puff stitch (puff) — three elongated half trebles drawn together. UK and US shared name.
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Do not turn. Three colours: A (centre), B (petals), C (border). Fasten off each colour at the end of its round and join the next.
Form a magic ring. Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). Work 18dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc to join. Pull tail to close ring. (18 dc.) Fasten off Colour A.

Join Colour B to any dc. *Ch 3. Work puff into next dc (yarn over, insert hook, pull up a long loop — repeat twice more into same dc, 7 loops on hook, yarn over and pull through all 7 loops, ch 1 to close). Ch 3. Sl st into next dc. Ch 1. Sl st into next dc.* Repeat from * to * eight more times. (9 petals, 9 sl st gaps.) Fasten off Colour B.

Join Colour C at any sl-st gap (between petals). Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Work 1 more tr into the same gap. Ch 1. *Into top of next puff work (2tr, ch 2, 2tr) for a corner. Ch 1. Work 2tr into next sl-st gap. Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * across two petal-top corners and two gap sets (6 corner repeats for the hexagon). At final repeat: into last puff work (2tr, ch 2, 2tr). Ch 1. Sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (48 tr, 6 ch-2 corner spaces, 12 ch-1 spaces.) Fasten off Colour C.

The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Round 1 forms the dc foundation. Round 2 shows nine puff petals alternating with sl-st gaps. Round 3 completes the hexagonal border with corner ch-2 spaces at six points.

definition.title: African flower — three colours
definition.caption: Three colour rounds. A: dc ring. B: nine puff petals with ch-3 arches. C: hexagonal treble border with ch-2 corners at six points.

content.text: Fasten off all three colour ends. Weave each tail through the back of the nearest round. Steam-block, pinning the six corners of the hexagonal border outward. The petals will settle into their full rounded shape with blocking.
Join through the ch-2 corner spaces and the ch-1 side spaces using

on the final round of each new motif, or whipstitch through the back loops of matching border stitches. Hexagons tile in a honeycomb grid; combine with the four-colour version (crochet-african-flower-four-colour) for a richer palette across the same grid.
Handwash in cool water with a small amount of mild soap, or machine-wash on a wool cycle. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat on a clean towel and ease to shape while damp.

The four-colour version (crochet-african-flower-four-colour) adds an extra border round for a 15 cm motif. The hexagon variant (crochet-african-flower-hexagon) produces a true hexagonal flower shape with a pointed border rather than the standard rounded-corner border.
